article_text:
EXCLUSIVE: Cannes award-winning French director Bruno Dumont has revealed his next feature The End is being made entirely using generative AI, without actors or a traditional film crew and on a shoestring budget.

The prolific auteur began work on the English-language sci-fi thriller in August and has since wrapped production, generating its images, performances and sound himself, with a festival rollout and theatrical release planned for 2027.

The End follows an ambitious Los Angeles police officer investigating a crime as the city is engulfed by earthquakes and falling asteroids. Set between contemporary Los Angeles and the Joshua Tree desert, the apocalyptic thriller charts the rise and fall of a man whose investigation takes on mystical dimensions.

Dumont said he wrote the screenplay more than 25 years ago, following 1999’s Humanity , but its elaborate disaster sequences made it prohibitively expensive to produce. The project was shelved, leading him instead to make his 2003 California-set drama Twentynine Palms . Generative AI technology has now made the project possible.

“The costs are on an entirely different scale compared to those of the traditional economy of the industry of cinema, said Dumont, who described the results as “astonishing”.

Dumont has dispensed with physical production altogether, generating the film’s images and sound from his Paris home while retaining control over the performances, mise-en-scène and editing. Rather than feeding the entire screenplay into an AI programme, he works scene by scene, using his own shot breakdowns to generate footage.

“I’m like a director working with a crew, except that my crew is a machine,” he said. “I give it instructions constantly.”

He said he can demand “greater emotional intensity or anger” from virtual actors and refine everything from sets and vehicles to costumes and hairstyles. He has also used faces from Flemish paintings as references, transforming them into contemporary characters.

Dumont, whose Humanity and Flanders won the Cannes Grand Prix in 1999 and 2006 respectively, is known for his unconventional filmmaking, often working with non-professional actors and blending realism with comedy and the surreal. His credits include Camille Claudel 1915 , starring Juliette Binoche, Cannes competition titles Slack Bay and France , and sci-fi satire The Empire , which won the Silver Bear jury prize at the 2024 Berlinale.

His latest feature, French Riviera-set coming-of-age tale Red Rocks , premiered in Cannes Directors’ Fortnight earlier this year before screening at San Sebastian and New York.

After struggling to secure French backing for Red Rocks , Dumont turned to other European territories. He is now producing The End independently, with no sales agent attached yet, and plans to seek festival premieres before pursuing distribution and international sales.

“With generative AI, auteur cinema can reclaim radical creative autonomy, bringing previously unachievable visual and poetic worlds to life, free from financial and industry constraints,” he suggested.

Dumont insisted the process is not fundamentally different from conventional filmmaking, with the machine generating material that he shapes through his own artistic decisions and sees AI as a route to artistic independence amid mounting difficulties financing auteur films in France.

“It is becoming harder and harder to finance films in France,” he said. “Today I have complete freedom. I can do what I want.”

Dumont is also developing a separate, conventionally financed French feature with human actors and film crews shot in live action with Nicolas Anthomé’s Bathysphere Films, the company behind Arthur Harari’s Cannes competition title The Unknown .

Mira Nair on “the beauty and struggle of independent cinema” and financing next film ‘Amri’

article_text:
Spain ’s Movistar Plus continues to double down on its strategies to further amplify Spanish series and storytelling internationally with the world premiere of the highly anticipated eco-thriller “ Patagonia .”

Bowing at the upcoming South International Series Festival in Cádiz, the series is the latest major co-production to be boosted by the Spanish streamer and the fruit of a pioneering collaboration with Chile ’s Wood Producciones and Spain’s Atlantika Films. Germany’s ZDF Studios handles international distribution for the series, which is set for release on Movistar Plus in January 2027.

Related Stories

Kevin Delaney Takes Role as NBC News' Head of Digital Content and Subscription

Led by “Money Heist” star Itziar Ituño, “Patagonia” is a six-episode series following Ituño’s Alicia, a desperate mother who travels from the Basque Country to Chile’s titular region to find her missing teenage son, Noah (Unai Arana).

As the search continues, Alicia must navigate her own family conflicts while dealing with the mysteries of the ancient forest and a dangerous illegal logging network. The series is created by Chilean writers María Elena Wood and Patricio Pereira. The former is behind Platino Prize best series winners “News of a Kidnapping” and “Dignity,” while the latter produced “Mary & Mike.”

“Patagonia” is directed by Rodrigo Susarte, who recently helmed the high-concept sci-fi “Hidden Island,” featured on this year’s Berlinale Series Market Selects. Speaking with Variety ahead of the film’s premiere, Susarte says he was drawn to the idea of an eco-thriller because it amplifies a suspense story’s core hook, which is “what we fail to see.”

“I didn’t want the series to explain the climate crisis,” he adds. “I’d rather it leaves the audience with a lingering sense of unease. Maybe the real question isn’t what we’re doing to the forest, but what part of ourselves disappears along with it.”

Wood adds that “Patagonia” was born from a desire “to tell a story in which a unique territory is not merely a backdrop, but a protagonist.” “We envisioned a contemporary Western set in the southern reaches of the globe—a place where extraordinary nature, isolated communities, economic interests, and deeply human conflicts coexist,” she notes.

Susarte mentions his work in the series was inspired by films by Werner Herzog and Jane Campion. The former is a particularly resonant influence given his infamous experience of shooting “Aguirre, the Wrath of God” in the depths of the Peruvian forest. When asked about the experience of shooting in Hornopirén, Susarte says it was a chance to physically experience how organisms can shape one another in nature.

“There, the forest isn’t a backdrop; it’s a presence, with its own rules, its own light, and its own sense of time,” he says. “The first thing you learn is that you’re not in charge. The weather rewrites your shooting schedule every morning, and there’s an almost philosophical lesson in learning to accept that without giving up. Filmmaking is, at its heart, an attempt to control things. Patagonia constantly reminds you where that control ends.”

The director also notes an interesting paradox that guided the shoot: “We were telling a story about the destruction of a forest while moving through it with an entire film crew.” “Shooting there demanded an awareness of the footprint we were leaving behind, of entering a space that doesn’t belong to us.”

“For me, bringing ‘Patagonia’ to life between Chile and Spain has been a truly unique experience, and undoubtedly one of the most rewarding projects of my career,” notes Atlantika Films producer Nano Arrieta. “Working alongside Pato and Mané at Wood Producciones has been a real privilege. From day one, we knew we were in excellent hands, with access to some of the finest crews in Chile. On the Spanish side, we made an equally strong commitment to bringing together top-tier talent in the Basque Country.”

The producer also mentions how “Patagonia” is feeding into an “incredibly exciting moment for Spanish cinema.” Arrieta brings up names like Oliver Laxe, Los Javis and Alauda Ruiz De Azúa as exponents of this new wave. “These are bold, distinctive filmmakers with powerful creative voices, and they’re helping push Spanish storytelling into exciting new territory.”

“Great moments in an industry usually come from something deeper than the market itself, [they come] from having confidence in your own voice,” adds Susarte. “I think that’s a big part of what’s happening in Spain right now. Stories that don’t feel the need to apologise for being local, and platforms like Movistar Plus have understood that. What I hope is that this moment doesn’t simply end with success, that it creates room for bolder creative voices, and that the dialogue between Spain and Latin America continues to grow.”

On top of launching “Patagonia,” Atlantika is currently developing “When Devils Rule,” a series based on an original idea by Arrieta and starring Oscar-nominated “Emilia Perez” actress Karla Sofia Gascón. “When Devils Rule” will also reunite Susarte and Ituño. The six-part series will be pitched at Tallinn’s TV Beats Co-Financing Market running Nov. 16-17.

“The concept is quite wild, actually. It’s a hyperrealistic story, deeply rooted in the political and social chaos of our times, but with one supernatural twist: demons,” says the producer of the series. “The central idea is pretty simple, and perhaps a little provocative. What if the political madness, moral corruption and sheer absurdity of the world we’re living in could only be explained by the fact that demons are actually behind it all?”

As for Susarte, he’ll soon start his festival journey with “Invunche,” a reinterpretation of a tale from Chilote mythology, originating in the Chiloé Archipelago in southern Chile and combining Indigenous beliefs with Spanish legends. “I’ve set it in a time when information reaches us in fragments, distorted and out of order. At the heart of it is the same idea I’ve always been drawn to: what does a place reveal about the people who inhabit it, and what does what we’re willing to lose reveal about us?”

Wood is currently developing two features, both international co-productions. “Arca” is directed by Matías Bize (“The Punishment”), written by Julio Rojas (“Case 63”), and co-produced with Spain’s Potenza, Brazil’s Trema, and Chile’s Céneca and Wood Productions. It is a psychological thriller that confronts its protagonists with an extreme moral dilemma in the face of a world spiraling out of control.

The second project, “Lucila,” is an animated feature film centered on the childhood of Gabriela Mistral in the Elqui Valley, exploring the emotional and creative world of the person who would go on to become one of the great voices of Latin American literature.

“Patagonia” is produced by María Elena Wood and Pereira and Atlantika’s Nano Arrieta and Claudia Ruiz. Production oversight is shared with ZDF Studios’ Sebastián Krekeler, Susanne Frank, and Peter Nadermann, plus Cristina Merino at Movistar Plus. “Patagonia” is an exclusive Movistar Plus series.

article_text:
Kathleen Kennedy , the former head of Lucasfilm, has been tapped as head of ceremonies and content for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.

She’s replacing Peter Rice, who was hired as Netflix’s chief content officer earlier this week and took over for Bela Bajaria. He will remain involved with the LA28 Games as executive producer, as first reported by the Hollywood Reporter .

In her role, Kennedy will lead the delivery of all four ceremonies, including the Olympics opening on July 14, 2028, and closing on July 30 as well as the Paralympic opening on Aug. 15 and closing on Aug. 27.

Related Stories

Where to Buy Tickets for Broadway's Biggest Shows Through 2027: 'Evita,' 'A Few Good Men,' 'Much Ado About Nothing' and More

LA28 chairperson and president Casey Wasserman called Kennedy a “legend” and “one of Hollywood’s all-time greats.”

“When the stars align to focus the world’s attention on Los Angeles for the 2028 Olympic and Paralympic Games, I can’t think of anyone better to conjure the magic of Hollywood than Kathleen,” he said.

Kennedy described the Olympics as “a touchstone in my life” and referred to the games as “one of the great unifying experiences we share.”

“Casey Wasserman has a bold vision for what these Games can mean for Los Angeles and the world, and I’m thrilled he’s asked me to help bring it to life,” Kennedy said. “My husband, Frank Marshall, and I have attended virtually every games since Los Angeles in 1984, and sport remains one of the great unifying experiences we share. Peter Rice has laid a terrific foundation, and I can’t wait to get to work with Ben Winston, our creative director, and the whole LA28 team.”

Kennedy left Lucasfilm at the end of 2025 after serving as president for 14 years. She maintains a relationship with the company behind “Star Wars” and “Indiana Jones,” with recent credits including last summer’s “The Mandalorian and Grogu” and the upcoming “Star Wars: Starfighter,” led by Ryan Gosling.

A widely respected producer, Kennedy worked closely with Steven Spielberg over the years on movies such as “E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial,” “Jurassic Park” and “Lincoln,” and she helped pick the director J.J. Abrams to helm 2015’s “Star Wars: The Force Awakens,” which successfully revived the franchise with more than $2 billion globally. Her tenure at Lucasfilm had both highs and lows, including misfires like 2018’s “Solo: A Star Wars Story” and 2023’s “Indiana Jones and the Dial of Destiny.”

article_text:
Through poetic narratives and bright hues Basim Magdy creates a world where the familiar slips into the surreal.

A deep sense of longing arises when experiencing Basim Magdy’s works. For his solo show in Istanbul, the artist probes the poetics and multilayered emotions that pass through one’s mind across works created between 2019 and 2026. Magdy has developed a distinctive visual language, expressed through vibrant colours and particularly in the fluidity between words and photography, as seen in Coming of Age in a Trembling Place (2023). The work comprises 16 photographs arranged in a grid, accompanied by four quotes drawn from the artist’s inner world. One reads, “I WAS IN MY EARLY TWENTIES WHEN I LEARNED THE LANGUAGE OF REGRET”. The emphasis on colour and the use of capital letters lend the text a particular intensity, almost like a bullet piercing the soul.

Among the four works on paper, The Rocket Scientist Who Believed He Was a Peacemaker (2026) marks Magdy’s return to the medium, which he last explored in 2013. The collage and painting showcase a mirrored scientist, divided between two opposing impulses. On the left, a hand detaches the rocket’s nose cone from its body; on the right, another hand becomes a pedestal for a bird. Magdy’s vibrant palette lends the composition a playful quality, with a disco ball that almost resembles the sun and, on the left, a form suggestive of either cave cones or glaciers. This visual playfulness gives way to the scientist’s underlying moral dilemma, caught between his consciousness and the belief that the rockets he creates might somehow bring about global peace. Magdy reinforces this tension through the deliberate arrangement of the composition, placing what might be read as the darker, destructive impulse on the left and the more peaceful, almost angelic gesture on the right. The mirrored figures give form to an internal struggle, where the aspiration to create and protect coexists with the capacity to destroy.

Throughout the exhibition, Magdy takes the viewer into a world of self-questioning, while the exhibition text itself reads almost like a confession, sharing an intimate walkthrough of the ideas and reflections that inform the artist’s practice. This personal account adds another layer to the works, revealing the thoughts and associations that surface behind their making. Created specifically for the exhibition, in A POEM (2026), 23 photographs are arranged in a row, which Magdy describes as “reminiscent of the lines of a poem or filmstrips”. In the accompanying text, he recounts a breakfast conversation with Bruce Jenkins in 2018, during which they discussed Bruce Conner’s experimental film A MOVIE (1958), which later became the starting point of A POEM . His enquiry focuses on the relationship between the survival of traces and the persistence of curiosity. Through photographs of marble quarries, historical artefacts, rocks and minerals, Magdy draws attention to the material traces through which human and geological histories are recorded. In a way, he suggests that history is not preserved simply because objects endure but because someone encounters those objects, asks questions about them and discovers meanings that were not anticipated. His photographs look as though they have been chemically altered, contrasting the elements within or perhaps creating an interplay in the overall scene.

A separate room is dedicated to The Birds Choose the Cards (2024), a film shot on 26 mm and transferred to HD media. In one scene, a visit to a fortune teller in Taipei becomes an attempt to understand the past, only to acknowledge that the present is already complicated enough. When the question of whether war will ever end arises, the response that it will only grow bigger introduces a further state of unease. Through layered images and sounds, Magdy moves between the sea as a site of migration and the spectacle of a colossal cruise ship, interspersing scenes of tourism with more unsettling references to war. The accompanying text references Plato’s allegory of the cave, stating, “We were prisoners chained and forced to look at shadows. The shadows become our light.”

Rather than making sense of the world, Magdy reveals the strange and often unsettling way in which we attempt to understand it. The eternal question remains, circling between the absurd and the profound, searching for meaning in the contradictions themselves.

2019–2026 AD: A Series of Disjointed Ideas Forming a Coherent Train of Thought runs until 24 October

article_text:
Dis/velamento La mostra personale di Marco Mezzacappa a cura di Lucrezia Febo

Dal 19 al 25 ottobre 2026 | Contart Lab, Via Candia 25, Roma

Dal 19 al 25 ottobre 2026, Contart Lab, in Via Candia 25 a Roma, ospita Dis/velamento, mostra personale di Marco Mezzacappa a cura di Lucrezia Febo. Il progetto espositivo invita il pubblico a immergersi nella ricerca pittorica dell’artista attraverso un percorso in cui spazio, materia e sguardo si intrecciano, dando vita a un’esperienza di progressiva scoperta.

Il titolo racchiude il principio che attraversa l’intera mostra: disvelare significa portare alla luce senza necessariamente rendere tutto visibile, rivelare lasciando aperta una zona di mistero. La pittura di Mezzacappa si sviluppa proprio in questa tensione tra presenza e assenza, rivelazione e sottrazione, invitando lo spettatore a interrogarsi su ciò che appare e su ciò che continua a sfuggire alla visione.

L’esperienza espositiva comincia prima ancora dell’incontro con le opere. Attraversando un portone, una navata e un cortile nascosto, il visitatore si allontana progressivamente dal rumore della città per raggiungere un ex studio fotografico, luogo raccolto e silenzioso che diventa parte integrante del progetto curatoriale. Il passaggio tra gli ambienti assume così il valore di una successione di soglie fisiche e percettive, capaci di modificare il ritmo della visita e predisporre a uno sguardo più attento e consapevole.

All’interno dello spazio, i dipinti di piccolo formato si presentano come frammenti e nuclei autonomi di una ricerca intima. Stratificazioni, sovrapposizioni, cancellazioni e tracce testimoniano un processo pittorico in continua trasformazione, nel quale ogni gesto conserva la memoria di quelli precedenti. La superficie diventa un luogo di sedimentazione del tempo, dove ciò che sembra scomparso continua a manifestarsi attraverso segni e presenze residue.

Il frammento assume un ruolo centrale: non è soltanto una parte incompleta, ma una possibilità aperta di visione. Anche il vuoto partecipa alla costruzione dell’immagine, trasformandosi in uno spazio di attesa e interpretazione. Le opere non offrono una narrazione immediatamente definita, ma invitano il pubblico a stabilire connessioni, ricomporre dettagli e costruire progressivamente un proprio percorso di lettura.

Il momento culminante della mostra è rappresentato da una grande opera figurativa, scomposta ma unita, nella quale la frammentazione incontra una possibile ricomposizione. La figura rappresentata di spalle introduce un ulteriore livello di riflessione sul rapporto tra osservatore e immagine: la sua postura richiama simbolicamente il gesto del visitatore che si volta, modifica il proprio punto di vista e torna a guardare ciò che ha appena lasciato alle proprie spalle.

In questa corrispondenza, il confine tra chi guarda e ciò che viene guardato si fa più sottile. La figura non si offre completamente allo spettatore, ma lascia spazio all’immaginazione e alla possibilità di interpretare ciò che rimane fuori dal campo visivo. Il gesto del voltarsi diventa così una metafora del processo conoscitivo: cambiare prospettiva significa aprirsi a nuove possibilità di vedere, riconoscendo che ogni immagine conserva una dimensione che non può essere interamente posseduta.

Con Dis/velamento, Marco Mezzacappa propone una riflessione sull’atto stesso del guardare. Vedere non significa necessariamente comprendere in modo immediato, ma accettare l’incertezza, sostare davanti all’immagine e lasciarsi coinvolgere dal suo lento manifestarsi. Il percorso espositivo accompagna il visitatore dalla città al silenzio, dalla distanza alla prossimità, dal frammento alla ricomposizione, trasformando l’incontro con la pittura in un’esperienza di attenzione e scoperta.

«Più si entra, più si vede. Ma più si vede, più emerge ciò che ancora non è stato visto.»

La mostra invita così a superare la superficie dell’immagine e a riconoscere nel disvelamento non una rivelazione definitiva, ma un processo continuo, nel quale ogni scoperta apre nuove domande e ogni soglia attraversata offre la possibilità di guardare diversamente.

article_text:
EXCLUSIVE: Maxine Peake has boarded The Secret Assistants , the BAFTA-qualifying short about an ambitious newcomer trying to make it in the movie business.

Katey Lee Carson writes and directs and, along with producing partner Rickie-Lee Roberts, channeled experience in the business into the short. Both have worked on major movies and their professional backgrounds informed The Secret Assistants .

Peake, whose credits include I Swear and The Theory of Everything , will be an exec producer on The Secret Assistants . “I wanted to be involved because, quite frankly, it’s a timely, urgent and brilliant film,” she said.

Related Stories

Himesh Patel & Maxine Peake Among The Stars In Latest Booker Prize Short Films

Ones To Watch: Milo Machado-Graner, 17, Reflects On 'Goodbye Cruel World' After 'Anatomy Of A Fall': "This Role Took Me To A Different Place"

The Secret Assistants follows Sophie, an ambitious newcomer navigating a high-stakes interview with an industry titan called Henry Mann. What begins as an opportunity to secure her future quickly spirals into a troubling power struggle, forcing Sophie to confront an impossible choice: challenge the ethical line she is being pushed to cross or risk jeopardizing everything she has worked so hard to achieve.

Watch on Deadline

The cast is led by Camille Rutherford ( Blue is the Warmest Colour ) as Sophie. Richard Hope ( Doctor Who ) plays Henry. Gina Stiebitz ( Dark ) and Emily Kusche ( Dogs of Berlin ) round out the cast.

Given the film’s focus on power imbalances and toxic work environments, its producers emphasized that everyone involved in its production was paid equally. Everyone from producer to runner got the same rate, they said.

The team behind The Secret Assistants said that although it is set in the entertainment business, its power imbalance and toxic workplace themes could apply to any sector or industry. The film is currently on a festival run that has taken in Busan International Short Film Festival, St Kilda Film Festival and HollyShorts.

"在我看来，《菲尔克特斯》（Thyestes）最具革命性之处就在于这个合唱团，它彻底颠覆了人们对“业余戏剧”的理解。通常情况下，戏剧中的“大众化”与业余成分会被当作一种引文或效果来使用，就像从舞台上跑过的鸡或牛，或是登场的杂技演员。业余性总是沦为一种导演手法，用来强化、支持真正的专业戏剧与剧情，或是对传统进行批判性的审视。但在这里并非如此。这个合唱团是在创作真正伟大的艺术。“这些是言语的乐谱、存在的乐谱。它们为舞台上的几位独奏者构成了框架，”莱维卡说道。因此，这种言语是一种能够真正触动人心的歌唱形式。", article_text:
Ein alter Freund, ein fast nackter Schauspieler und eine antike Tragödie über Tyrannei, Gewalt und den Zerfall der Welt: In Schwerin zeigt die Regisseurin Joanna Lewicka, wie politisch Theater sein kann – gerade jenseits der großen Bühnenmetropolen

Eigentlich wollte ich nur meinen alten Freund Frankie auf der Bühne sehen. Frankie, oder Frank Büttner, ist in meinem Alter, wie ein Ost-Spiegelbild von mir. Wir beide haben einen narzisstischen Knall, sind von den Subkulturen im eingemauerten Berlin geprägt – eben nur auf verschiedenen Seiten. Wir beide lieben die Kunst und hatten ein tolles, aber nicht ganz einfaches Leben.

Im Gegensatz zu mir war Frankie allerdings Calvin-Klein-Model in New York und lief für Helmut Lang, als es noch wirklich cool war, während ich noch Wave-Bars putzte. Wenn wir uns treffen, können wir bei einer Pizza wie Schwestern über alles reden, eben über unser sehr tolles Leben, das Älterwerden , den Tod, Herzschmerz, den fucking Rechtsruck, auch in der Kultur.

Und natürlich über Frankies zweite Karriere: Fast sein gesamtes Erwachsenenleben hat er als forensischer Therapeut gearbeitet – und dabei noch eine Karriere als Schauspieler an der Volksbühne hingelegt, unter seinem Freund Frank Castorf. Er ist quasi eines der Gesichter der alten Volksbühne; die Kamera des deutschen Arthouse liebt ihn. Er ist aber auch ein neues altes Gesicht in diesem Mix aus Theater, bildender Kunst und Performance, der gerade der heißeste Scheiß in der Kunstwelt ist.

Nackt angesichts des drohenden Faschismus

Wenn Frankie eine Frau wäre, würde er bestimmt bei Florentina Holzinger nackt auf einem Motorrad oder einem Jetski rumknattern. Aber weil er ein Mann ist, verkörperte er 2024 in Ersan Mondtags Beitrag für den deutschen Pavillon, "Monument eines unbekannten Menschen", Mondtags Großvater Hasan Aygün, der aus einem armen Dorf östlich von Ankara in den 1960er-Jahren nach Westberlin kam. Über 30 Jahre arbeitete er in der Firma Eternit, fertigte Baumaterialien aus Asbest und starb kurz nach der Pensionierung an Lungenkrebs. Frankie stellte ihn nackt im Leichentuch dar, wie es sich für ein menschliches Monument gehört.

Und auch bei Ersan Mondtags Performance-Projekt "Alternde Meister" in der Gemäldegalerie zum Auftakt der Berlin Art Week war er natürlich wieder fast nackt, verletzlich, physisch superpräsent. Es ist komisch, wie in den Sixties und Seventies, aber diesmal kommt keine Revolution, keine Utopie, sondern Faschismus 2.0, und alle ziehen sich aus Protest aus.

Jetzt tritt Frankie wieder ziemlich nackt auf, schwebt auf Projektionen völlig nackt herum, wie der Riesenembryo in Kubricks "2001: Odyssee im Weltraum". Nicht im Berliner Ensemble oder am Broadway, sondern im Theaterzelt des Mecklenburgischen Staatstheaters in Schwerin, dessen Haus gerade renoviert wird. Er sagte mir schon vor geraumer Zeit, dass er dahin wolle, denn dort gebe es eine neue Schauspieldirektorin, Joanna Lewicka, die total spannend inszeniere.

Wichtige Fragen mal nicht in Berlin-Mitte stellen

Die aus Polen stammende Theaterregisseurin hat international gearbeitet und findet gerade große Resonanz, weil sie vieles wirklich anders macht. 2024 bekam sie den Deutschen Theaterpreis Der Faust, die renommierteste und wichtigste Auszeichnung in Deutschland, für ihre Inszenierung der "Antigone" am Theater Plauen-Zwickau. Sophokles fragt in seiner Tragödie von 442 v. Chr. nach dem Recht des Einzelnen auf Widerstand gegen den Staat. Wo sind die Grenzen der Selbstbestimmung des Individuums und wo die Grenzen der Staatsgewalt?

Natürlich toll, diese Frage nicht in Berlin-Mitte zu stellen, sondern dort, wo viele Menschen sich genau in der Rolle dieses Individuums sehen und die Nation wie in Geiselhaft der bürgerlichen Parteien und des westlichen Establishments empfinden. Lewicka geht mit ihren Inszenierungen in die sogenannte Provinz, nach Sachsen, Detmold oder jetzt eben nach Schwerin – an Orte, wo das Theater eine ganz andere, wie ich denke, viel politischere Rolle spielt als in den Großstädten, mit Besucherzahlen, Budgets und reaktionären Auffassungen kämpft und manchmal unter regelrecht prekären Bedingungen arbeiten muss.

Ihre Interpretationen griechischer Tragödien oder Shakespeare-Dramen nutzen nie trendige Verweise auf aktuelle politische Ereignisse, illustrieren nicht, sondern kochen diese eigentlich zeitlosen politischen oder existenziellen Fragen elementar herunter. Sie macht dabei das Theater sowohl für die Schauspieler als auch für das Publikum zu einer körperlichen, emotionalen und einmaligen Erfahrung, an der alle für einen Moment teilhaben.

Theater der Grausamkeit 2.0

Ein wichtiger Bezug ist die eigentlich lange totgesagte Vision von Artauds "Theater der Grausamkeit", das nicht lediglich Blut, Kotze und Sadismus meint, sondern Grausamkeit im Sinne von Lebensgier, von kosmischer Unerbittlichkeit, erbarmungsloser existenzieller Notwendigkeit, die elementar zu jedem Leben gehört. Angesichts der brennenden Erde und der alten korrupten Männer, die eine Art Endzeit beschwören und noch alles raffen und ausbeuten, was nur geht, um sich in Bunker zu retten, kann diese Grausamkeit wohl jeder nachvollziehen. Wir alle wollen verschont bleiben, vergebens.

Grausam geht es auch im "Thyestes" zu, einer ziemlich unbekannten Tragödie des römischen Stoikers Seneca (1 n. Chr.–65 n. Chr.), mit deren Premiere Lewicka wenige Tage nach dem Wahlsieg der AfD in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern ihren Einstand in Schwerin machte. Sehr passend behandelt das Stück die Tyrannei Einzelner über die Welt, die aufgrund ihrer wahnsinnigen Grausamkeit völlig aus den Fugen gerät und der Apokalypse entgegensieht. Senecas "Thyestes" gilt als das stoische Lehrstück über die zerstörerische Natur unkontrollierter Affekte und die Pervertierung politischer Macht.

Das Interessante daran ist, dass Seneca nicht nur literarische Vorlagen hatte, sondern dem legendären Tyrannen Nero von dessen Jugend an als Berater diente und dafür seine stoischen Ideale über Bord warf. Nero, der ihn zu einem der reichsten Männer des Römischen Reichs machte, zwang ihn später aufgrund der vermeintlichen Teilnahme an einem Putsch zum Selbstmord.

Abgeschlachtet, ausgeweidet, zerstückelt

Dabei ist das Lehrstück ein Familiendrama: Die Brüder Atreus und Thyestes sind die Enkel des Tantalus und von Geburt an mit einer Blutschuld belastet. Gemeinsam ermordeten sie einst ihren Halbbruder Chrysippos, um den Thron von Mykene zu besteigen. Doch Thyestes hintergeht seinen Bruder, betrügt ihn mit seiner Frau und stiehlt mit ihrer Hilfe das Goldene Vlies – das göttliche Widdersymbol der Herrschaft. Dafür wird er verbannt. Doch sein Bruder Atreus sinnt auf Rache. Unter dem Vorwand der Versöhnung lockt er Thyestes zurück nach Mykene und bietet ihm die gemeinsame Herrschaft an. Thyestes ist misstrauisch, doch willigt ein. Um die Versöhnung zu feiern, will Atreus ein Opfer darbringen. Doch die Opfer sind Thyestes' Söhne, die Atreus abschlachtet, ausweidet, zerstückelt und Thyestes als Festmahl serviert. Beide verlieren angesichts dieser ungeheuren Grausamkeit den Verstand, die Sonne verdunkelt sich, die kosmische Ordnung ist gestört, das Grauen setzt sich fort.

Also keine leichte Kost, nicht gerade der Stoff, um das Publikum, das Volk, abzuholen wie an einer Bushaltestelle, die zu Kultur und Demokratie führt. Kein Stück, das Hoffnung spendet oder Gräben zuschüttet, eher eine Absage daran. Zum Glück. Denn am Premierenabend vollbringt Lewicka so etwas wie ein Wunder: Sie erreicht mit diesem harten, komplexen und archaischen Stück wirklich alle, schafft fast so etwas wie einen offenen Raum, ein Theatermysterium.

Nicht nur Artaud liefert da den Treibstoff, sondern auch Castorf, dessen Einfluss man spürt. Das fängt mit Frankie an, der zu Beginn als Geist des verfluchten Tantalos auftritt, frisch aus dem Hades, wohin ihn die Götter zu ewigem Hunger und Durst, zu ewiger Angst in einem See verbannt haben, weil auch er ihren Nektar stahl und ihnen dann seinen eigenen Sohn zum Essen vorsetzte. Frankie spielt diesen Geist in Rage, der auch seine Nachkommen verflucht, mit unglaublicher physischer Präsenz, mit Schreien und Flüstern, begleitet von einer Pole-Dancing-Furie (Svetlana Belesova). Das Publikum liebt diese Szene.

Aus den Trümmern von Artaud und Castorf

Und natürlich ist da auch ein Hauch von Castorfs postironischem Regiestil, genauso wie bei Astrid Meyerfeldt (Atreus) und Norbert Stöß (Thyestes), die beide eng mit der Volksbühne verbunden sind. Beide spielen umwerfend, regelrecht atemberaubend, zwischen Slapstick, Wahnsinn und absoluter Verletzlichkeit. Doch aus den Trümmern von Artauds Denken und des legendären Castorf-Theaters, das immer auf einer gewissen genialischen Männlichkeit und Schlauheit bestand, schafft Lewicka etwas Neues: ein Theater der Dringlichkeit und Teilhabe.

Auf die Frage, ob dieses Stück über Tyrannei nicht zu pessimistisch als Start ihrer Arbeit in Schwerin sei, antwortet sie: "Ich bin davon überzeugt, dass wir an das Gute glauben müssen, weil wir ansonsten sofort aufhören müssten zu existieren. Aber gleichzeitig befinden wir uns in einer so großen Distanz zu uns selbst, dass alles hoffnungslos erscheint. Für mich ist das eine ganz, ganz wichtige Entscheidung, das genauso zu erzählen. Wir können uns jetzt nicht mehr länger belügen."

Genau dieses Gefühl vermittelt ihr "Thyestes", der nicht auf der verbreiteten deutschen Fassung von Durs Grünbein beruht, sondern auf der roheren und poetischeren Neufassung des Belgiers Hugo Claus, die 1966 entstand, als Artaud gerade seine Hochphase im Theater hatte. Das Bühnenbild hat den Tempel der Herrscher in eine Art Kellerloch transformiert. Durch eine aufgebrochene Wand blickt man in eine behelfsmäßige, zusammengestückelte Küche, darunter ein improvisiertes, dystopisches Thronzimmer.

Hoffnung in der Hoffnungslosigkeit

"Wir fangen eigentlich in einer Küche bei einer Familie an", sagt Lewicka. "Und die Größe, das Ausmaß der Gedanken dieser Menschen greift in das Weltgeschehen ein, in das Machtgefüge. Für mich ist dies eine feine Gratwanderung, die das Stück thematisiert: Wie sehr wirkt diese Familie nach innen, aber auch nach außen? Und wie werden Hass und Gewalt zum alltäglichen Gegeneinander?" Der Gedanke, dass die Tyrannei an unseren Küchentischen, in unseren dysfunktionalen Familien entsteht, dass Tyrannen aus unserem Umgang miteinander, unserem Sprechen und Handeln geboren werden, dass ein Rückzug ins Private keine Erlösung vom politischen Wahnsinn ist, ist zentral für diese Inszenierung. Es heißt, dass nicht nur Kriege und Morde am Küchentisch beginnen, sondern auch politischer Wandel. Es zählt, was wir denken und tun – oder nicht tun. Mehr, als wir denken. Das ist die Hoffnung in diesem eigentlich hoffnungslosen Stück.

Besonders deutlich wird das durch den Chor, der das Stück einbettet. Er setzt sich aus Mitgliedern der Schweriner Singakademie und Statisten zusammen, darunter viele Schülerinnen und Schüler zwischen 16 und 18 Jahren, allesamt Laien, allesamt Leute, die sich mit der poetischen und harten Sprache auseinandersetzen müssen. Sie schreiten durch die Gänge, zivil, ohne Kostüme, in den Raum und sprechen synchron Sätze wie: "Nutzlos dreht sich das gewaltige Rad durch die Zeit, denkt an die Familien, die sich gegenseitig zerreißen, an niedergebrannte Paläste, Königreiche, die verschwinden wie der Tau, an die ständig schweigenden, stets fliehenden Götter, an die Völker, die gefoltert werden und geschlachtet wie Schafe."

Das Tolle daran ist, dass sie sprechend denken, nicht nur über den Inhalt, sondern auch über die Sprache, ihre eigene Stimme – und dass sie das zusammen wie eine Art Schwarm machen, quasi vielstimmig und dann doch wie eine Stimme.

"Partituren des Sprechens"

Für mich ist das Revolutionäre am "Thyestes" dieser Chor, der das, was man unter "Laientheater" versteht, völlig auf den Kopf stellt. Normalerweise wird das "Volkstümliche", Laienhafte im Theater wie ein Zitat oder Effekt eingesetzt, so wie Hühner oder Kühe, die über die Bühne laufen, oder Akrobaten, die auftreten. Immer dient das Laienhafte als Regieeinfall, der das eigentliche professionelle Theater, die Handlung, verstärkt, unterstützt oder Konventionen kritisch hinterfragt. Hier nicht. Dieser Chor macht wirklich große Kunst. "Es sind Partituren des Sprechens, des Seins. Sie bilden den Rahmen für einige wenige Solisten auf der Bühne", sagt Lewicka. Dieses Sprechen ist also eine Form von Gesang, die wirklich berührend sein kann.

Als der Chor angesichts der Schlachtung der Kinder vielstimmig Sätze singt wie: "Ist dies der Augenblick? Sind wir es, nach allen Generationen auf der Erde, die es verdient haben, zu vergehen? Verdient haben, zerschmettert zu werden vom herabstürzenden Himmel?", geschieht etwas. Zumindest bei mir. Dieses vermeintliche Kellerloch auf der Bühne erinnert plötzlich an den Anblick zerbombter Häuser, deren Fassaden fehlen, in denen die Familien öffentlich in ihren kaputten Wohnzimmern, den Ruinen ihrer Schuld oder Unterdrückung, leben und kochen. Ich denke an das zerbombte Berlin, natürlich an die Ukraine und Gaza. "Meine Gäste von der polnischen Presse, mit denen ich mich gestern unterhalten habe, haben darin ganz klar die polnisch-deutsche Geschichte und die Zerstörung Warschaus im Zweiten Weltkrieg gesehen", sagt Lewicka. "Aber all diese Lesarten haben etwas gemeinsam: den Hass und eine Gewalt, die immer weiter eskaliert."

Lewickas große Leistung ist es, eine dringliche, zugleich offene Form des Theaters zu entwickeln, die nie didaktisch oder besserwisserisch wird, sondern neue und durchaus demokratische Erfahrungen schafft – an Orten, wo es nicht einfach ist. Das tut sie ohne genialische Attitüde, mit einer existenziellen, empathischen Haltung, die erstaunlich gut in die Jetztzeit passt. "Theater ist eine vergängliche Kunst", sagt sie. "Eine Kunst, die stirbt, so wie der Mensch selbst. Wir hinterlassen keine Bilder. Wir hinterlassen keine Musikkomposition, die wir uns 20 Jahre später anhören können. Wir hinterlassen einen ganz, ganz starken Moment des Erlebens, der das Theater so einzigartig macht. Dieser Moment des Sterbens birgt auch eine ganz große Chance, in ihm Lebendigkeit zu erfahren."

"维维安·萨森（以下简称VS）：摄影的可能性是无限的。这只是一种视角，也可能是多种视角，或许是另外100种或1000种视角。解读永远是无数的。我本人也是这样看待自己的照片的。一张影像，几乎就像是一个单独的词汇。当它与其他词汇或影像并置时，就会组成句子，诞生新的故事。但如果把这个词从语境中抽离出来，和另一张照片并置，意思就会改变，从而能够创造出又一个故事。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "——也就是说，作品的意义并未被固定，而是向观者开放的吗？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "VS：对我而言，“模糊性”和“矛盾”这两个词自始至终都非常重要。我一直被那些令我感到困惑的影像所吸引。因为无法理解，所以才更想去探究。或者说，在感受到强烈情感的同时，又完全不清楚它到底意味着什么。正是这样的影像才会留在心底。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://imaonline.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/2B2A9689-1000x674.jpg", "alt": "2B2A9689", "caption": "", "credit": "IMA", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "不以政治之眼，而以诗意之眼", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "——包括时尚在内，您在各种语境下都进行过创作。如今，影像如何被消费正变得非常不稳定。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "VS：在创作作品时，特别是在艺术创作中，我尽量不去考虑这一点。如果是商业工作，我会非常灵活。为了让客户满意并解开那个谜题，自我会有所退让。但在艺术创作中，我可以做自己喜欢的事。在创作时，我会触及潜意识，顺其自然、凭直觉行动。我不会去考虑观者，而是去思考是什么在驱使着我。去探索自己的执念，追逐自己的阴影与光明。我试图用一种如同孩童般开放的、充满好奇心的眼光去看待世界。解读和政治，全都是随后来到的。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "——现在每个人都被要求表明自己的政治立场。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "――许多年轻创作者将“我的故事、我的身体、我的身份”这一自传领域当作安全区。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "VS：我认为这是一个问题。归根结底，大家都只会盯着自己的肚脐眼看。摄影师尤其必须要走出去。如果所有人都退守到自己的角落里，对世界而言是没有好处的。这是一个不断试错的过程。这个房间里的许多作品都是在2000年代初期、20年前、25年前拍摄的。当时围绕表征和文化挪用的讨论远没有现在这么激烈。能有这些讨论是一件非常好的事情。但特别是在网络上，讨论变得过热且被简化了。灰色地带和模糊性因此而丧失了。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我坚信，一个事物可以具有多种含义，绝不能被还原为单一的事物。因此，对于当年的作品，我至今仍旧承载着它们。如果问我现在是否还会做同样的事，我会采取不同的做法。但当时我是怀着真诚的心去创作的。我也犯过错误。不过，犯错也是可以的。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://imaonline.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/2B2A9720-1000x687.jpg", "alt": "2B2A9720", "caption": "", "credit": "IMA", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "霍勒太太——年长女性的力量", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "――在新作中，通过道具、拼贴画以及直接的摄影，展现了不同年龄段女性的身体。这是一个怎样的项目？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "VS：这是最新的项目《Frau Holle》。这是我与好友、荷兰艺术家埃梅琳·德·莫伊共同创作的。在20世纪90年代相遇的时候，我们就曾去森林里，只是单纯地玩耍和实验。而数十年后的今天，我向她发出邀请，希望能再次开启那份共同创作。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "霍勒太太是对欧洲异教古老民间故事的一种致意。格林兄弟也曾记述过她的故事，但更古老的民间故事是关于年老女性力量的故事。在许多文化中，年长的女性都被置于社会边缘，变得隐形。西方媒体中展现的，要么是年轻漂亮的女孩，要么是年长的男性。而且长期以来，女巫作为对社会的威胁而被架上火刑柱。她们拥有智慧。不再生育。或者选择从社会中退隐，独自生活。这对于社会、尤其是对于男性而言，是一种威胁和恐惧。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "有趣的是，这个系列中包含着大量的幽默，也有着蓬勃的情色力量。爱欲，也就是生命力。不仅仅是性的力量，更是生命本身的力。从来没有哪个系列引发过如此两极分化的反响。有人说非常喜欢，也有人直视无能。人们无法直视年长、热烈、强大且具有性吸引力的女性，这一事实本身就说明了很多问题。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://imaonline.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/321a99513664ea2294b5ebfaec9c7e43-1024x683.png", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "IMA", "translated": "——女性生殖器位置长着一张嘴巴的作品令人感到震惊。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "VS：这非常直白，但也有点像吐舌头那样，带有一点“去你的”的意味。这是一种叛逆的行为。并不是因为她以性感的姿态展示自己——因为色情内容到处都是。相反，在这里是由她掌握着主导权，向观者伸出手，或者发出一声嘲笑。我们只是在享受乐趣。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "——回归神话的冲动是从何而来的呢？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "VS：这不是刻意为之的。我们两人从一开始就被它深深吸引。例如，埃梅琳一直在研究“谢拉纳吉格”（Sheela na Gig）。那是中世纪日耳曼和爱尔兰文化中，被放置在教堂或建筑物顶部的简朴雕像，描绘了一个老妇人用双手撑开自己生殖器的形象。正如印度的时母卡莉（Kali）一样，她既是恶也是善。这是一个粗粝的影像，但其含义在于她将生与死融为一体。这是生命的循环。在系列中，也出现了印有“Vulva（女性器）”而非“Volvo（沃尔沃）”字样的蓝色T恤。", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "生动鲜活，无所畏惧", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "——萨森女士的许多作品都涉及女性身体，这与您的时尚工作是如何结合的呢？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "VS：时尚在很多情况下是关于美、年轻和审美的。不过对我而言，去探索另一条道路同样重要。作为一个女性，能够保持生动鲜活、无所畏惧。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "日本文化中最让人惊叹的一点是，女孩们从很小的时候就被教导要举止文静，甚至表现得有些羞涩。比如用手捂着嘴说话，那种某种程度上顺从的仪态。这非常美丽，我也对这种文化怀有深深的敬意。但与此同时，我也觉得这是一个非常父权制的社会。正因如此，去挑战那道边界才是一件畅快的事。我相信女性内在的力量、创造力以及情色力量，能够将其表达出来是一件非常美丽的事。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://imaonline.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/2B2A9765-625x422.jpg", "alt": "2B2A9765", "caption": "", "credit": "IMA", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "――据说由荷兰书籍设计师伊尔马·布姆（Irma Boom）操刀的摄影集《Frau Holle》也引发了截然相反的反响。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "VS：它或许不会像其他书那样卖得那么快。不过，我希望它能作为一种具有小众崇拜色彩的存在，找到属于自己的道路。世界上有一种趋向安全稳妥的倾向。如果那样的话，一切都会变得千篇一律。那多无趣啊。请去承担风险。不要在意保持安全。这才是人生，这才是活着。去承担风险，去探索。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Viviane Sassen｜维维安·萨森 1972年出生于荷兰阿姆斯特丹。童年在肯尼亚度过的经历，塑造了她独特的色彩感以及对光影的敏锐感知。她横跨静物、肖像与风景，确立了几何抽象与身体表现相交织的视觉语言。她活跃于缪缪（Miu Miu）、路易威登（Louis Vuitton）、迪奥（Dior）等时尚界以及《Purple》、《Dazed & Confused》等杂志，将时尚与艺术视作一脉相承的实践。主要摄影集有《Flamboya》（2008年）、《Umbra》（2014年）、《Of Mud and Lotus》（2017年）。曾参与纽约现代艺术博物馆的“New Photography”（2011年）、威尼斯双年展（2013年），并于2023年在欧洲摄影之家（巴黎）举办大型回顾展。2024年参与了KYOTOGRAPHIE京都国际摄影节。2026年出版与埃梅琳·德·莫伊的合著《Frau Holle》（Kominek Books，设计：伊尔马·布姆）。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": article_text:
東京・神宮前のThe Massで個展「Myriads（無数）」を開催中のオランダの写真家、ヴィヴィアン・サッセン。2000年代初頭の初期作、未発表作品、そして友人のアーティスト、エメリン・デ・モーイとともに古い民話の女神を現代に呼び戻した新シリーズ《Frau Holle》（ホレおばさん）が展示されている。ファッションとアートを往還しながら撮られてきたイメージは、ひとつの意味に還元されることを拒み、政治ではなく詩の眼で世界を見つめ直すためにあるという。イメージの多義性、政治化する時代の表現、そして年を重ねた女性の力をめぐり、話を聞いた。

ポートレイト撮影＝高木康行 取材・文＝アイヴァン・ヴァルタニアン

目次

一枚のイメージは一つの言葉のように

政治の眼ではなく詩の眼で

フラウ・ホレ――年を重ねた女性の力

生々しく、臆さずに

一枚のイメージは一つの言葉のように

――展覧会タイトルの「Myriads」は、とても開かれた言葉ですね。

ヴィヴィアン・サッセン（以下、VS） ：写真の可能性は無限です。これはひとつの視点にすぎないし、いくつもの視点かもしれないし、もう100や1000の視点なのかもしれません。解釈はいつも無数にある。私自身、自分の写真をそう捉えています。一枚のイメージは、ほとんど一語の単語のようなもの。ほかの言葉やイメージと並ぶと文になり、新しい物語が生まれる。でもその言葉を文脈から取り出し、別の写真と並べれば、意味は変わり、また別の物語をつくることができるのです。

――作品の意味は固定されず、見る人に開かれているということでしょうか。

VS ：私にとっては「曖昧さ」と「矛盾」という二つの言葉が、昔からとても大切です。私はずっと、自分を戸惑わせるイメージに惹かれてきました。理解できないから、もっと探りたくなる。あるいは強い感情を受け取るのに、何を意味しているのか完全にはわからない。そういうイメージこそが心に残るのです。

政治の眼ではなく詩の眼で

――ファッションを含め、さまざまな文脈で仕事をされてきました。イメージがどう消費されるかは、いまとても不安定です。

VS： 作品をつくるとき、特にアートの作品では、そのことは考えないようにしています。商業の仕事なら、とても柔軟です。クライアントを満足させ、そのパズルを解くために、自我は一歩引かせる。でもアートでは、自分の好きなことができる。制作するときは潜在意識に触れ、流れるように、直感的に動きます。見る人のことは考えず、自分を突き動かすものについて考える。自分の執着を探り、自分の影と光を追いかける。子どものように開かれた、好奇心に満ちた眼で世界を見ようとしています。解釈や政治は、すべて後から来るものです。

――いまは誰もが政治的な立場を示すことを求められています。

VS： いまの世界では、あらゆるものが政治的になってしまって、とても舵取りが難しい。それが人を怖がらせ、内側へ引きこもらせる。外の世界や未知のもの、他者と関わることが怖くなってしまうのです。すべてが政治的だとわかっていても、私はそこから距離を置き、驚きをもって世界を見たい。政治の眼ではなく、詩の眼で。

――若い作家の多くは「私の物語、私の身体、私のアイデンティティ」という自伝的な領域を安全地帯にしています。

VS： それは問題だと思います。突き詰めれば、みんな自分のへそばかり見つめることになる。写真家は特に、外へ出ていかなければなりません。みんなが自分の隅に引きこもったら、世界のためにはならないでしょう。試行錯誤なんです。この部屋の作品の多くは2000年代初頭、20年、25年前に撮ったものです。当時は表象や文化の盗用をめぐる議論は、今ほど強くなかった。こうした議論があるのはとても良いことです。でも特にオンラインでは、議論が過熱し、単純化されてしまう。グレーゾーンが、曖昧さが失われるのです。

ひとつのものが複数の意味をもちうる、ひとつのことに還元などできない、と私は強く信じています。だから当時の作品を、今も引き受けています。今なら同じことをするかと聞かれたら、違うやり方をするでしょう。でもあのときは誠実な心でつくった。間違いもしました。でも、間違えてもいいのです。

フラウ・ホレ――年を重ねた女性の力

――新作では、小道具やコラージュ、ストレートな写真を通して、さまざまな年代の女性の身体が表されています。どのようなプロジェクトですか。

VS： 最新のプロジェクト《Frau Holle》です。友人でオランダのアーティスト、エメリン・デ・モーイとの共同制作です。1990年代に出会った頃、私たちは森へ行き、ただ遊び、実験していました。そして何十年も経った今、その共同作業をもう一度始めようと彼女に声をかけたのです。

フラウ・ホレは、異教の古いヨーロッパの民話への目配せです。グリム兄弟も彼女の話を書き留めていますが、もっと古い民話は、老いた女性の強さについての物語なのです。多くの文化で、年配の女性は社会の外側に置かれ、見えない存在になっていく。西洋のメディアに映るのは、若くてきれいな女の子か、年上の男性ばかりです。そして長いあいだ、魔女は社会の脅威として火あぶりにされてきた。彼女たちは知恵をもっていた。もう子どもを産まない。あるいは社会から身を引いて、ひとりで生きることを選んだ。それは社会にとって、とりわけ男性にとって、脅威であり恐怖だったのです。

面白いことに、このシリーズにはユーモアがたくさんあり、エロティックな力もたくさんある。エロス、つまり生命力です。性的なものだけでなく、生命そのものの力。これほど反応が分かれたシリーズは初めてです。大好きだという人もいれば、まともに見ることができない人もいる。年を重ねた、激しく強く性的な女性を人々が直視できないということ自体が、多くを物語っています。

――女性器の位置に口がある作品には驚かされました。

VS： とてもあからさまですが、舌を突き出すような、ちょっとした「くたばれ」でもあるんです。反抗的な行為。彼女が性的な存在として自分を見せていることが、ではありません。ポルノはどこにでもあふれていますから。そうではなく、ここでは彼女が主導権を握り、見る者に手を伸ばし、あるいは嘲笑っている。私たちはただ楽しんでいるのです。

――神話へ立ち返る衝動はどこから来るのでしょう。

VS： 意識的なものではありません。二人とも最初からずっと惹かれてきたものです。たとえばエメリンは「シーラ・ナ・ギグ」を研究していました。中世のゲルマンやアイルランドの文化で、教会や建物の上部に置かれた、老女が両手で自らの女性器を押し広げる素朴な像です。インドの女神カーリーのように、悪でもあり善でもある。荒々しいイメージですが、その意味は、彼女が生と死をひとつに抱えているということ。生命の円環なのです。シリーズにも、「Volvo」ではなく「Vulva（女性器）」と書かれた青いTシャツが出てきます。

生々しく、臆さずに

――サッセンさんの作品の多くは女性の身体を扱っていますが、ファッションの仕事とはどう結びついているのでしょうか。

VS： ファッションは多くの場合、美や若さ、美学についてのものです。ただ私にとっては、別の道も探ることが大切なのです。女性として、生々しく、臆さずにいられるということ。

日本の文化で特に驚かされるのは、とても小さい頃から女の子が控えめに、ほとんど恥ずかしがるように振る舞うよう教えられることです。手で口元を隠して話すような、どこか従順な振る舞い。それはとても美しいし、この文化を深く尊敬しています。でも同時に、とても家父長的な社会だとも思う。だからこそ、その境界に挑むのは気持ちがいいのです。女性の内にある力、創造的でエロティックな力を私は信じていますし、それを表現できるのはとても美しいことです。

――オランダのブックデザイナー、イルマ・ブームが手がけた写真集『Frau Holle』への反応も分かれているそうですね。

VS： ほかの本ほど早くは売れないでしょう。でも、小さなカルト的な存在として、自分の道を見つけていってくれたらと思います。世界には、安全で無難な方へ向かう傾向がある。そうするとすべてが同じになってしまう。そんなのは退屈です。リスクをとってください。安全でいることを気にしないで。それこそが人生であり、生きるということです。リスクをとり、探求すること、です。

Viviane Sassen｜ヴィヴィアン・サッセン 1972年、オランダ・アムステルダム生まれ。幼少期をケニアで過ごした経験が、独自の色彩感覚と光と影への感性を形づくった。静物、ポートレイト、風景を横断し、幾何学的な抽象と身体表現が交差する視覚言語を確立。ミュウミュウ、ルイ・ヴィトン、ディオールなどのファッションや『Purple』『Dazed & Confused』などの雑誌でも活躍し、ファッションとアートを地続きの実践として捉える。主な写真集に『Flamboya』（2008年）、『Umbra』（2014年）、『Of Mud and Lotus』（2017年）。ニューヨーク近代美術館「New Photography」（2011年）、ヴェネチア・ビエンナーレ（2013年）に参加し、2023年にはヨーロッパ写真美術館（パリ）で大規模な回顧展を開催。2024年にはKYOTOGRAPHIE 京都国際写真祭に参加した。2026年、エメリン・デ・モーイとの共著『Frau Holle』（Kominek Books、デザイン：イルマ・ブーム）を刊行。

article_text:
Os projetos vencedores da Bolsa ZUM/IMS 2026 são Na noite escura, escuto clarões , de Rafael RG ; e Mundos-Gavinhas , de Uýra .

Os projetos serão avaliados por uma comissão constituída por curadores do Instituto Moreira Salles, além de convidados externos com trabalhos reconhecidos na área fotográfica e audiovisual. Serão consideradas a qualidade artística, a qualificação do candidato e a viabilidade prática do projeto.

A comissão julgadora, composta pelas curadoras e pesquisadoras Beatriz Lemos e Clarrisa Diniz, Daniele Queiroz, curadora da área de Arte Contemporânea do IMS e Thyago Nogueira, coordenador da área de Arte Contemporânea do IMS, selecionou os ganhadores depois de avaliar mais de 850 projetos de todas as partes do país. Os contemplados receberão bolsas de R$80 mil, e desenvolverão seus projetos durante oito meses, orientados pela área de Arte Contemporânea do IMS. Parte do resultado será incorporada à Coleção de Arte Contemporânea do IMS, ao lado dos projetos vencedores em anos anteriores.

Em Na noite escura, escuto clarões , Rafael RG investigará parte do acervo fotográfico do Observatório Nacional para aproximar imagens históricas do céu e histórias de fuga de pessoas negras escravizadas no Brasil. A partir do estudo de placas de vidro do século XVIII, que registravam acontecimentos astronômicos, e o cruzamento de dados de fuga de pessoas negras escravizadas, a pesquisa entende o céu como arquivo, rota e tecnologia de sobrevivência.

Em Mundos-Gavinhas , Uýra se inspira nas tecnologias coletivas das florestas, pesquisando vínculos entre comunidades de plantas e pessoas. Com imagens de vegetais, arquivos históricos e testemunhos orais, o projeto percorre cidades para refletir sobre memória e regeneração, celebrando os vínculos que sustentam a Vida e os caminhos que ela encontra para ressurgir em tempos de devastação.

“Movendo-se entre performance, fotografia, vídeo e ativismo, Uýra vai mergulhar em diferentes territórios e costurar sua história com a de outras vozes, arquivos e movimentos sociais. Suas investigações desobedecem às divisões hierárquicas entre os seres e nos convidam a reimaginar as formas de viver — e conviver — na terra”, comenta Clarissa Diniz.

Na visão de Beatriz Lemos, “o projeto de Rafa RG nos impacta ao transformar o céu em arquivo, rota e tecnologia de sobrevivência. Ao cruzar dados históricos de fugas de pessoas escravizadas com o acervo fotográfico do Observatório Nacional, a pesquisa revela como a astronomia e a memória negra se entrelaçam na luta pela liberdade. Nosso júri está honrado em premiar uma investigação tão urgente e poética.”

A arte da edição 2026 da Bolsa ZUM/IMS foi criada pelo designer Oga Mendonça

Conheça os artistas e projetos vencedores das edições anteriores:

Desde 2014 a Bolsa ZUM/IMS convida pesquisadores, curadores e artistas ligados ao campo da imagem para compor o corpo de jurados do prêmio. Confira a lista com os convidados em cada ano:

title_original: France Riots Put Hollywood Shoots on Alert as Curfews Disrupt Movie Theaters: It ‘Has Now Been Flagged as a Problem Area’
editorial_title_zh: 法国骚乱拉响了好莱坞拍摄警报并导致影院宵禁干扰：现已“被标记为问题区域”
editorial_excerpt_zh: 正值法国迎来两部电视界最具魅力且充满逃避现实色彩的国际热门剧集——Netflix《艾米丽在巴黎》（Emily in Paris）最终季以及HBO《白莲花度假村》（The White Lotus）第4季——之际，该国却遭受了数十年来最暴力的骚乱冲击……

"https://variety.com/2026/tv/global/ben-frow-exiting-chief-content-officer-5-skydance-uk-network-1236911166/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在里昂，骚乱者纵火焚烧了贝勒库尔广场（Place "在这场末日般的景象中，法国继续充当好莱坞几大制作的游乐场，特别是在法国里维埃拉地区，该地区正在进行迈克·怀特（Mike White）《白莲花度假村》第四季的最后阶段拍摄。华纳兄弟的《十一罗汉》（Ocean）前传正在摩纳哥收尾法国部分的拍摄，该片由布拉德·库珀（Bradley Cooper）执导并与玛格特·罗比（Margot Robbie）、乔治·麦凯（George "text": "到目前为止，这些制作基本没有受到干扰，但骚乱已经让电影剧组感到不安，并促使好莱坞各大制片厂的安全部门发出了警告。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "资深法国执行制片人拉斐尔·贝诺利尔（Raphaël Benoliel）目前正在尼斯参与《Pumping Black》的工作，他表示尽管拍摄尚未受到干扰，但美国团队对暴力事件感到担忧。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“美国人确实问过，‘你们觉得危险吗？’我们告诉他们，‘从我们所在的地方来看，我们觉得挺好的。’一切都进展顺利，”贝诺利尔说。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "但谈到即将到来的拍摄时，动荡可能会影响未来对目的地的决定。“制片厂内部安全部门明确表示，‘小心点。避开巴黎。避开马赛，’”贝诺利尔说。“这是明确传达过的。如果你今天或明天想在巴黎组织一次外景勘测，制片厂完全有可能会说，‘不，推迟吧。等等。’”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "他接着说道：“由于发生的事情，法国现在已被标记为一个问题区域。你知道人们怎么说吗，‘现在不要去乌克兰拍电影’，或者不去中东某些地方？好吧，现在法国已经被列入了那个名单。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "不过，贝诺利尔表示，法国南部——除了马赛之外——受骚乱的影响并不像巴黎或里尔这样的大城市那么严重。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“当你看着电视上发生的事情时，你会有一种不一定能反映实地真实情况的印象，”他说。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "高蒙影业（Gaumont）高管伊莎贝尔·德戈尔日（Isabelle Desgorges）表示，暴力事件也吓坏了住在尼斯的剧组人员，那里的商店在周末遭到洗劫，她的团队正在负责《十一罗汉》前传的制作服务。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“我的整个剧组都住在尼斯，所以有点恐慌，尤其是因为这是一部美国大电影。人们想知道这到底是怎么回事，”德戈尔日说。“但幸运的是，我们周六和周日没有拍摄，我们的剧组也没有直接卷入暴力事件；他们是从远处看到的。尽管如此，这还是营造了一种奇怪的氛围。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "该片于7月下旬在巴黎开始拍摄，随后向南转移到摩纳哥，目前正在那里完成拍摄，之后还将在比利时的一个水箱进行几天额外的拍摄。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "德戈尔日担心，在社交媒体和新闻频道上蔓延的暴力画面可能会让美国制片人暂时对目前在法国工作感到退缩。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“我不会说美国人再也不想来法国了。但不可避免地，这会在几周内产生一些紧张情绪，”她说。“幸好这不是发生在7月。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "骚乱发生之际，法国正迎来国际制作活动激增的热潮，尤其是在法国南部。仅戛纳截至9月上旬就已记录了310个拍摄日，其中包括《白莲花度假村》和《艾米丽在巴黎》的工作。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "法国的电影院也感受到了余波，特别是在实施了宵禁的市中心。自周一以来，马克龙已下令在包括巴黎、马赛、里昂、里尔、利摩日和波尔多等主要城市在内的地方实施局部夜间宵禁。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "法国全国电影院联合会（FNCF）主席理查德·帕特里（Richard Patry）表示，“大约有20到30家影院受到宵禁措施的影响”，但他强调法国拥有约2500家电影院，这为影迷提供了充足的选择。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“显然，这产生了一定影响，但根本无法量化。我能告诉你的唯一一件事是，截至周二结束的那一周，与去年同期相比增长了12%，”他说。“受到直接影响的电影院可以通过对比平时的观影人数与现在的实际人数来计算损失，但在其他所有地方，这几乎是不可能的。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在巴黎，宵禁正在影响大堂电影院（UGC Ciné Cité Les Halles），这家庞大的巴黎综合影院按观影人次计算是全球最繁忙的影院之一。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "该综合影院已将最后一场放映时间提前至晚上7点，以便观众在宵禁前回家。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“当然，这是一个极其重要的电影院，提早关门确实会产生影响。由于宵禁，有些人就不去那里了。这是现实，”帕特里说道。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "法国租金追踪公司（Rentrak France）的埃里克·马蒂（Eric Marti）表示，这些骚乱恰逢周六的观影人次比前一个周末减少了大约10万，考虑到这标志着学校假期的开始，这是一个格外令人失望的结果。“我们本该做得更好，”他说。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "但观影热潮在次日反弹，周日观影人次比前一个周日增加了8万。“出现了一种追赶效应，”马蒂说。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "上周的一些大片包括由文森特·兰顿（Vincent Lindon）和塔哈·拉希姆（Tahar Rahim）主演的制片公司（Studiocanal）的《悲惨世界》（Les Miserables），该片开画周末表现缓慢，在第一周设法售出了480,822张票。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "据帕特里称，截至周二结束的那一周，总体观影人次实际上比去年同期增长了12%，而自2026年年初以来，法国票房已增长了26%以上。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“尽管正在发生这一切，尽管局势如此令人焦虑，人们仍然想去电影院。而且他们也确实去了，”他说。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "目前，随着极右翼和激进左翼政党在民调中领先，电影院线经营者和制片人都在密切关注，暴力事件是否会在总统大选临近之际成为一个反复出现的问题。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这个周末注定又将活动满满，周六将再次举行全国性抗议活动，这一次将有军事力量在场。然而，一些重大现场活动仍在按计划进行，尤其是美国国家橄榄球联盟（NFL）于周日在新奥尔良圣徒队和匹兹堡钢人队之间在巴黎举行的首场比赛。几天后，席琳·迪昂（Céline Dion）曾在此演出的雅高竞技场（Accor Arena）仍定于10月29日举办马克利摩尔（Macklemore）的“自由巴勒斯坦”（Free Palestine）巡演。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "如果说有什么能证明现场娱乐活动在混乱中依然能够蓬勃发展，那便是迪昂。上周六，迪昂得以在法国首都完成她复出驻唱的第一阶段，并回到了紧邻香榭丽舍大街的五星级蒙索皇家酒店（Royal Monceau），在那里，包括路易威登（Louis Vuitton）和迪奥（Christian Dior）在内的奢侈品精品店的橱窗被砸碎，商品被盗。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这位加拿大巨星还发现自己意外地被卷入了法国的政治争论之中，此前法国总统埃马纽埃尔·马克龙（Emmanuel Macron）及其妻子布里吉特（Brigitte）在骚乱前夕出席了她的音乐会。他们的这次公开出游在法国媒体上受到了批评，这对总统夫妇被指责对民情麻木不仁，甚至在法国大革命前夕被拿来与路易十六（Louis XVI）和玛丽·安托瓦内特（Marie-Antoinette）作比较。", "translated": true}]
article_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "In the same year that France has hosted two of television’s most glamorous and escapist international hits — the final season of Netflix’s “ Emily in Paris ” and Season 4 of HBO’s “ The White Lotus ” — the country has been shaken by one of its most violent waves of rioting in decades.", "links": [{"text": "Emily in Paris", "url": "https://variety.com/t/emily-in-paris/"}, {"text": "The White Lotus", "url": "https://variety.com/t/the-white-lotus/"}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "What began as nationwide demonstrations on Oct. 17 over the rising cost of living and deteriorating conditions in public schools descended into scenes of urban chaos. Some 550,000 people took to the streets and the protests turned into widespread looting, arson and clashes with police. Three days later, authorities had recorded 2,397 arrests, and at least 3,000 businesses have been damaged alongside landmarks."}, {"type": "heading", "text": "Related Stories"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://variety.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/ben-frow-1000.jpg?w=250&h=167&crop=1", "alt": "LONDON, ENGLAND - MARCH 12: Chief Content Officer, 5, Ben Frow attends the launch event for \"5\", uniting Channel 5 and streaming service My5 under one brand  on March 12, 2025 in London, England. (Photo by Darren Gerrish/WireImage for 5/Paramount)", "caption": "", "credit": "Variety · Film"}, {"type": "heading", "text": "Ben Frow Stepping Down as Chief Content Officer of 5, Skydance's U.K. Network, After 14 Years", "links": [{"text": "Ben Frow Stepping Down as Chief Content Officer of 5, Skydance's U.K. Network, After 14 Years", "url": "https://variety.com/2026/tv/global/ben-frow-exiting-chief-content-officer-5-skydance-uk-network-1236911166/"}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "In Lyon, rioters set fire to the historic tourist office on Place Bellecour. In Marseille, masked protesters stormed City Hall and toppled a bust of Marianne, the symbol of the French Republic. In Paris, luxury boutiques were ransacked and storefronts smashed."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Amid the post-apocalyptic spectacle, France has continued to serve as a playground for some of Hollywood’s biggest productions, notably in the French Riviera region, which is hosting the final stretch of filming on the fourth season of Mike White’s “The White Lotus.” Warner Bros.’ “Ocean” prequel, which Bradley Cooper is directing and starring in opposite Margot Robbie, George MacKay and Monica Barbaro, is wrapping its French shoot in Monaco; and Mimi Cave’s psychological thriller “Pumping Black,” starring Natalie Portman, Jonathan Bailey and Lukas Gage, is filming in Nice."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "So far, these productions have largely escaped disruption, but the riots have rattled film crews and prompted warnings from Hollywood studios’ security departments."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Veteran French executive producer Raphaël Benoliel, who is currently working on “Pumping Black” in Nice, says the American team was concerned about violence even though the shoot hasn’t been disrupted so far."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“The Americans did ask, ‘Do you think it’s dangerous?’ We told them, ‘From where we are, we think it’s fine.’ And everything has been going smoothly,” Benoliel says."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "But when it comes to upcoming shoots, the unrest might impact future decisions over destinations. “The studios’ internal security departments have clearly said, ‘Be careful. Avoid Paris. Avoid Marseille,’” Benoliel says. “That has been explicitly communicated. If you wanted to organize a location scout in Paris today or tomorrow, it’s entirely possible that a studio would say, ‘No, postpone it. Wait.’”"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "He continues, “Because of what happened, France has now been flagged as a problem area. You know how people say, ‘Don’t go filming in Ukraine right now,’ or in certain parts of the Middle East? Well, now France has been put on that list.”"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Still, Benoliel says the South of France — with the exception of Marseille — hasn’t been as affected by the riots as big cities like Paris or Lille."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“When you watch what’s happening on television, you get an impression that doesn’t necessarily reflect the reality on the ground,” he says."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The violence also spooked crew members staying in Nice, where shops were looted over the weekend, says Isabelle Desgorges, a Gaumont executive whose team is handling production services on the “Ocean’s” prequel."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“My entire crew is staying in Nice, so there was a bit of panic, especially because it’s a big American movie. People were wondering what on earth was going on,” Desgorges says. “But fortunately, we weren’t filming on Saturday or Sunday, and our crew wasn’t directly caught up in the violence; they saw it from a distance. Still, it creates a strange atmosphere.”"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The production began filming in Paris in late July before moving south to Monaco, where it is completing its shoot ahead of a few additional days filming at a water tank in Belgium."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Desgorges is worried the images of violence spreading on social media and news channels could temporarily give American producers cold feet about working in France for the time being."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“I wouldn’t go so far as to say that Americans no longer want to come to France. But inevitably, it’s going to create some tension for a few weeks,” she says. “It’s a good thing that this isn’t happening in July.”"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The riots comes at a time when France has been enjoying a surge in international production activity, particularly in the South of France. Cannes alone had logged 310 filming days by early September, including work on “The White Lotus” and “Emily in Paris.”"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The fallout is also being felt by France’s movie theaters, particularly in city centers where curfews have been introduced. Since Monday, Macron has ordered localized nighttime curfews in major cities, including Paris, Marseille, Lyon, Lille, Limoges and Bordeaux, among others."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Richard Patry, president of France’s National Federation of French Cinemas (FNCF), says “around 20 to 30 theaters are being affected by curfew measures,” but stresses France counts around 2,500 cinemas, which gives moviegoers plenty of alternatives."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“Clearly, there has been an impact, but it’s impossible to quantify. The only thing I can tell you is that the week ending Tuesday was up 12% compared with the equivalent week a year ago,” he says. “The cinemas that have been directly affected can calculate their losses by comparing their usual attendance with what they’re seeing now, but everywhere else, it’s virtually impossible.”"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "In Paris, the curfew is impacting the UGC Ciné Cité Les Halles, the sprawling Paris multiplex which ranks among the world’s busiest cinemas by admissions."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The multiplex has moved its last screening to 7 p.m. to allow moviegoers to return home before the curfew."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“Of course, it’s an extremely important movie theater, and closing earlier has an impact. Some people aren’t going there because of the curfew. That’s a reality,” Patry says."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Eric Marti at Rentrak France says the riots coincided with a drop of approximately 100,000 admissions on Saturday compared with the previous weekend, an especially disappointing result given that it marked the beginning of the school holidays. “We should have done better,” he says."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "But moviegoing rebounded the following day, with Sunday admissions rising by 80,000 compared with the previous Sunday. “There was a catch-up effect,” Marti says."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Some of the big releases last week included Studiocanal’s “Les Miserables,” starring Vincent Lindon and Tahar Rahim, which had a slow opening weekend and managed to sell 480,822 tickets in its first week."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Overall admissions for the week ending Tuesday were actually up 12% compared with last year, while French box office has been up more than 26% since the beginning of 2026, per Patry."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“Despite everything that’s happening, despite how anxiety-inducing the situation is, people still want to go to the cinema. And they’re going,” he says."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "For now, both exhibitors and producers are watching closely to see whether the violence will become a recurring problem in the run-up to the presidential election, with the far right and radical left parties leading in polls."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "This weekend promises to be once more packed with action, with another day of nationwide protests slated for Saturday, this time in the presence of military forces. Yet, some major live events are going ahead as planned, notably the NFL’s first game in Paris between the New Orleans Saints and Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday. article_text:
In the same year that France has hosted two of television’s most glamorous and escapist international hits — the final season of Netflix’s “ Emily in Paris ” and Season 4 of HBO’s “ The White Lotus ” — the country has been shaken by one of its most violent waves of rioting in decades.

What began as nationwide demonstrations on Oct. 17 over the rising cost of living and deteriorating conditions in public schools descended into scenes of urban chaos. Some 550,000 people took to the streets and the protests turned into widespread looting, arson and clashes with police. Three days later, authorities had recorded 2,397 arrests, and at least 3,000 businesses have been damaged alongside landmarks.

Related Stories

Ben Frow Stepping Down as Chief Content Officer of 5, Skydance's U.K. Network, After 14 Years

In Lyon, rioters set fire to the historic tourist office on Place Bellecour. In Marseille, masked protesters stormed City Hall and toppled a bust of Marianne, the symbol of the French Republic. In Paris, luxury boutiques were ransacked and storefronts smashed.

Amid the post-apocalyptic spectacle, France has continued to serve as a playground for some of Hollywood’s biggest productions, notably in the French Riviera region, which is hosting the final stretch of filming on the fourth season of Mike White’s “The White Lotus.” Warner Bros.’ “Ocean” prequel, which Bradley Cooper is directing and starring in opposite Margot Robbie, George MacKay and Monica Barbaro, is wrapping its French shoot in Monaco; and Mimi Cave’s psychological thriller “Pumping Black,” starring Natalie Portman, Jonathan Bailey and Lukas Gage, is filming in Nice.

So far, these productions have largely escaped disruption, but the riots have rattled film crews and prompted warnings from Hollywood studios’ security departments.

Veteran French executive producer Raphaël Benoliel, who is currently working on “Pumping Black” in Nice, says the American team was concerned about violence even though the shoot hasn’t been disrupted so far.

“The Americans did ask, ‘Do you think it’s dangerous?’ We told them, ‘From where we are, we think it’s fine.’ And everything has been going smoothly,” Benoliel says.

But when it comes to upcoming shoots, the unrest might impact future decisions over destinations. “The studios’ internal security departments have clearly said, ‘Be careful. Avoid Paris. Avoid Marseille,’” Benoliel says. “That has been explicitly communicated. If you wanted to organize a location scout in Paris today or tomorrow, it’s entirely possible that a studio would say, ‘No, postpone it. Wait.’”

He continues, “Because of what happened, France has now been flagged as a problem area. You know how people say, ‘Don’t go filming in Ukraine right now,’ or in certain parts of the Middle East? Well, now France has been put on that list.”

Still, Benoliel says the South of France — with the exception of Marseille — hasn’t been as affected by the riots as big cities like Paris or Lille.

“When you watch what’s happening on television, you get an impression that doesn’t necessarily reflect the reality on the ground,” he says.

The violence also spooked crew members staying in Nice, where shops were looted over the weekend, says Isabelle Desgorges, a Gaumont executive whose team is handling production services on the “Ocean’s” prequel.

“My entire crew is staying in Nice, so there was a bit of panic, especially because it’s a big American movie. People were wondering what on earth was going on,” Desgorges says. “But fortunately, we weren’t filming on Saturday or Sunday, and our crew wasn’t directly caught up in the violence; they saw it from a distance. Still, it creates a strange atmosphere.”

The production began filming in Paris in late July before moving south to Monaco, where it is completing its shoot ahead of a few additional days filming at a water tank in Belgium.

Desgorges is worried the images of violence spreading on social media and news channels could temporarily give American producers cold feet about working in France for the time being.

“I wouldn’t go so far as to say that Americans no longer want to come to France. But inevitably, it’s going to create some tension for a few weeks,” she says. “It’s a good thing that this isn’t happening in July.”

The riots comes at a time when France has been enjoying a surge in international production activity, particularly in the South of France. Cannes alone had logged 310 filming days by early September, including work on “The White Lotus” and “Emily in Paris.”

The fallout is also being felt by France’s movie theaters, particularly in city centers where curfews have been introduced. Since Monday, Macron has ordered localized nighttime curfews in major cities, including Paris, Marseille, Lyon, Lille, Limoges and Bordeaux, among others.

Richard Patry, president of France’s National Federation of French Cinemas (FNCF), says “around 20 to 30 theaters are being affected by curfew measures,” but stresses France counts around 2,500 cinemas, which gives moviegoers plenty of alternatives.

“Clearly, there has been an impact, but it’s impossible to quantify. The only thing I can tell you is that the week ending Tuesday was up 12% compared with the equivalent week a year ago,” he says. “The cinemas that have been directly affected can calculate their losses by comparing their usual attendance with what they’re seeing now, but everywhere else, it’s virtually impossible.”

In Paris, the curfew is impacting the UGC Ciné Cité Les Halles, the sprawling Paris multiplex which ranks among the world’s busiest cinemas by admissions.

The multiplex has moved its last screening to 7 p.m. to allow moviegoers to return home before the curfew.

“Of course, it’s an extremely important movie theater, and closing earlier has an impact. Some people aren’t going there because of the curfew. That’s a reality,” Patry says.

Eric Marti at Rentrak France says the riots coincided with a drop of approximately 100,000 admissions on Saturday compared with the previous weekend, an especially disappointing result given that it marked the beginning of the school holidays. “We should have done better,” he says.

But moviegoing rebounded the following day, with Sunday admissions rising by 80,000 compared with the previous Sunday. “There was a catch-up effect,” Marti says.

Some of the big releases last week included Studiocanal’s “Les Miserables,” starring Vincent Lindon and Tahar Rahim, which had a slow opening weekend and managed to sell 480,822 tickets in its first week.

Overall admissions for the week ending Tuesday were actually up 12% compared with last year, while French box office has been up more than 26% since the beginning of 2026, per Patry.

“Despite everything that’s happening, despite how anxiety-inducing the situation is, people still want to go to the cinema. And they’re going,” he says.

For now, both exhibitors and producers are watching closely to see whether the violence will become a recurring problem in the run-up to the presidential election, with the far right and radical left parties leading in polls.

This weekend promises to be once more packed with action, with another day of nationwide protests slated for Saturday, this time in the presence of military forces. Yet, some major live events are going ahead as planned, notably the NFL’s first game in Paris between the New Orleans Saints and Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday. A few days later, the Accor Arena, where Céline Dion performed, is still due to host Macklemore’s “Free Palestine” tour on Oct. 29.

And if there was any proof that live entertainment events could still thrive amid the chaos, it was Dion. Last Saturday, Dion was able to wrap the first leg of her comeback residency in the French capital and return to the five-star Royal Monceau hotel right by the Champs-Élysées avenue, where luxury boutiques including Louis Vuitton and Christian Dior had their windows smashed and merchandise stolen.

The Canadian superstar had also found herself unexpectedly drawn into France’s political debate after President Emmanuel Macron and his wife Brigitte attended her concert on the eve of the riots. Their social outing drew criticism in the French media as the presidential couple was accused of being tone-deaf, and were even compared to Louis XVI and Marie-Antoinette on the eve of the French Revolution.

article_text:
Films and events

Dare

Hearing

Thính giác

Known for his precise and enigmatic filmmaking, here Lê Bảo crafts a meditative anti-love story revealing fragile connections between humans, sounds and unseen worlds.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director-screenwriter Lê Bảo

With Nguyễn Quốc Tuấn, Ngọc Tản, Khánh Huyền

Vietnam-Singapore-Norway-France-Indonesia-Saudi Arabia-Cambodia-Thailand-Taiwan 2026. 128min

Courtesy of Heretic

Language Vietnamese With English subtitles

Introduction

Working as a decibel-reader technician, Ninh encounters hidden sonic tensions within the world around him, from uneasy presences in a cemetery to the restless rhythms of a zoo. Through these encounters, the film transforms the everyday into moments of unexpected drama and tenderness. Utilising his signature style – meticulous framing and minimalist performances – Bảo expands his formalism into an open, emotionally resonant cinematic experience.

Hyun Jin Cho

Content advice

Contains scenes of nudity and sex.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

A Day in the Life of Jo: Chapter Phaedra

Jacqueline Lentzou follows Moon 66 Questions with this evocative and playful look into the life of a teenager who is completely unaware of the forces at play in her fate.

Supporting Role

This mysterious and uniquely introspective journey through Tbilisi traces the steps of a once-famous Georgian actor.

The Calf Doll

When his only cow delivers a stillborn calf and then falls sick, a retired professor turns to an age-old calf-doll ritual, while industrialisation closes in around him.

title_original: MMCA×LG OLED Series 2026
summary_zh: 韩国国立现代美术馆首尔馆展览《MMCA×LG OLED Series 2026》，官网展期 2026-07-31 至 2026-11-29；票价、开放日与预约请核对原文。

editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "此时此刻，我们在首尔展厅（Seoul Box）内，这里是韩国国立现代美术馆（National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art, Korea）的一个标志性空间。该空间目前正举办“MMCA×LG OLED”系列展的第二届展览，该系列于去年首次推出。这一合作项目由韩国国立现代美术馆与 LG 电子（LG Electronics）联合策划。通过将先进的显示技术与艺术想象力相结合，该系列为参观者提供了体验当代艺术的新方式。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在本年度的展览中，艺术家克里斯蒂娜·孙·金（Christine Sun Kim）利用首尔展厅的建筑特点，通过大型数字动画与墙面绘画创作了一件纪念碑式的装置作品，从而转换了这一空间。艺术家克里斯蒂娜·孙·金是一位常驻柏林的韩裔美国人，她通过绘画、动态影像和表演等多种媒介，探索了语言、声音以及沟通结构。她在当代艺术界获得了广泛认可，包括在英国一家当代艺术杂志发布的2025年国际当代艺术最具影响力人物榜单中位列第34位。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "金发展出了一种独特的艺术语言，将日常交流的语言转化为视觉形式。她的作品根植于聋人群体的经验，汲取了广泛的视觉元素，包括美国手语、乐谱、漫画书的运动线条、手绘图画、图表以及文字。通过这些元素，金在视觉上揭示了语言如何塑造和转化人际关系，以及它如何将我们与广阔的世界联系在一起。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "她的作品邀请我们重新审视那些常常被我们视为理所当然的沟通系统与惯例。近年来，她的创作已从单一的绘画和表演扩展到沉浸式的空间环境，将语言本身转化为一种三维体验。在这个空间里，我们被邀请去体验语言在多重感官中是如何产生、流动并碰撞的。", "translated": true}]

article_text:
Here in the Seoul Box, we are standing in a symbolic space of the National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art, Korea. This space currently hosts the second exhibition of the MMCA×LG OLED Series, which launched for the first time last year. This collaborative project was developed by the National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art, Korea in partnership with LG Electronics. By combining advanced display technology and artistic imagination, this series offers visitors new ways of experiencing contemporary art.

For this year's edition, artist Christine Sun Kim has transformed this space by utilizing the architectural characteristics of the Seoul Box to create a monumental installation consisting of large-scale digital animation and wall drawings. Artist Christine Sun Kim, a Berlin-based Korean American, has explored language, sound, and structures of communication across a diverse range of media, including drawing, moving image, and performance. She has gained significant recognition in the contemporary art world, including being ranked 34th on a 2025 British contemporary art magazine list of the most influential figures in international contemporary art.

Kim has developed a distinctive artistic language that translates communicative language into visual form. Rooted in the experiences of deaf communities, her work draws upon a wide range of visual elements, including American Sign Language, musical notation, the motion lines of comic books, handwritten drawings, diagrams, and text. Through these elements, Kim visually reveals how language forms and transforms interpersonal relationships, and how it connects us to the world at large.

Her work invites us to reconsider the systems and conventions of communication that we often take for granted. In recent years, her practice has expanded beyond individual drawings and performances into immersive spatial environments, transforming language itself into a three-dimensional experience. Within this space, we are invited to experience the ways in which language is generated, moves, and collides through multiple senses.

editorial_excerpt_zh: “关于真实性的问题如今已经过时了” Saskia Trebing Wed, 10/21/2026 - 12:11
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "艺术家诺埃米·尼诺（Noémie Ninot）在约会软件上询问男性关于理想女性的特征。由此诞生了一系列面具，揭示了我们自我形象的人为性", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "诺埃米·尼诺，在你的作品中，你探讨了男性对理想女性有着怎样的想象，以及这些想象是如何在约会资料和照片中反映出来的。当我们不断迎合他人对我们的想象时，我们的自我形象会发生什么变化？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我在Hinge、Tinder和Bumble等各种不同的约会软件和网站上，就异性恋顺性别男性心目中的理想女性形象询问了他们的看法，尤其是关于外表Appearance的方面。我收集了300条回答，将其分类并记录在一个Excel表格中。在此分类的基础上，诞生了30幅肖像作品，这些幻想通过乳胶面具得以成形。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "为什么选择面具？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "因此，乳胶面具成了一种规范化、通常是刻板印象的理想的载体，它可以被字面意义上地戴上。通过将这些人工塑料面孔具象化，该系列作品质疑了男性欲望的建构、“理想女性”的集体想象，以及它对我们西方视觉文化所说明的问题。这些肖像试图回应这些原型，却又永远无法真正达到它们。在这些影像中，对自我的想象一次又一次地走向失败，也正因如此，它才变得清晰可见。", "translated": true}, {"type": "quote", "text": "在Instagram上查看此快讯 Ninot (@noemieninot) 分享的快讯", "links": [{"text": "Sieh dir diesen Beitrag auf Instagram an", "url":
